title: Column: AI usage patterns may be shifting the case for self-hosted servers
snippet: A new Anthropic threat intelligence report offers an unusual glimpse into how advanced AI systems are being used under heavy, real-world workloads. The findings suggest that the decision to buy or host AI servers may depend less on model quality alone, and more on which tasks consume tokens, how long they run, and how much operational state they must preserve.

title: AMAX expands liquid-cooled data center in push beyond hardware
snippet: Amax is expanding its self-built liquid-cooled data center as the company moves beyond hardware into infrastructure and engineering services, with customer demand giving it more than a year of order visibility.

title: US-Mexico trade talks put AI servers in focus as Taiwan ODMs seek common ground
snippet: The US is reportedly pressuring Mexico to tighten rules of origin for AI hardware to limit the use of components produced outside North America, particularly in China. Server supply chain sources said the Mexican government began consultations with Taiwanese original design manufacturers (ODMs) around 10 days ago to explore mutually acceptable solutions, signaling a willingness to negotiate.

title: DIGITIMES Insight: AI chip upgrades shift substrate supply bottleneck from upstream materials to equipment
snippet: DIGITIMES Intelligence has observed that as the performance of AI accelerators and server CPUs continues to advance, chips are increasing not only in compute core counts and I/O channels but also in integration complexity. title: Dassault Systèmes: AI-native transformation emerges as Taiwan's next industrial frontier
snippet: Digital transformation is no longer the endpoint for Taiwan's technology industries. As artificial intelligence moves from individual applications into core business operations, companies are entering a new phase in which AI, engineering models, and industrial knowledge are increasingly integrated into product development and operations, Dassault Systèmes said.

title: HEC Compucase AI server products drive 2026 revenue growth
snippet: HEC Compucase's AI server-related rollout continues to gain traction as AI racks, cooling modules, and high-end power supplies move into mass production or volume shipments. The company expects fourth-quarter 2026 shipments and operating momentum to strengthen further, with full-year 2026 revenue set to maintain double-digit growth and first-half gross margin rising to 24%, about 3 percentage points higher than a year earlier.

title: ACES targets AI compute and power with cable ramp-up
snippet: High-speed transmission demand continues to rise on the back of AI server and data center buildouts, while cloud service providers (CSPs) accelerate adoption of in-house application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) platforms. As a result, demand for high-speed connectors and high-speed transmission cables inside servers is also increasing.

title: Tyntek optical communications MPD ramps quarterly, 2027 capacity triples
snippet: Tyntek is rapidly expanding into optical communications as AI data-center demand drives a surge in high-speed transmission needs, with shipments set to rise significantly from the third quarter and gross margin and profitability expected to improve sharply. Backed by clear orders from a major US customer, the company has already launched an NT$1.2 billion (US$37.7 million) expansion plan approved by its board in August, aiming to triple monthly capacity to 1,500 wafers by the end of 2027.

title: Samsung reportedly cuts QD TV output 80% as Neo QLED phaseout looms
snippet: Samsung Electronics will reportedly slash quantum-dot (QD) LCD TV production in 2026 to 2 million to 3 million units, down as much as 80% year-over-year, while it also plans to gradually scale back Neo QLED output and potentially stop production as early as 2028. The move shifts the company's LCD TV focus toward Mini LED models without QD.

title: Ampoc AI PCB orders surge as it expands into CPO
snippet: Printed circuit board (PCB) wet-process equipment maker Ampoc Far-East said demand for its in-house high-end equipment has surged on AI servers and high-performance computing applications, driving brisk orders in the first half of 2026 and strong utilization rates. Capacity is now close to fully booked, and customers have also begun laying out long-term orders for the next one to two years.

title: AI safety debate heats up: Pegatron chairman urges risk controls, not an innovation halt
snippet: AI safety concerns are intensifying debate over whether development should slow, with US technology executives divided over the trade-off between innovation and risk. Pegatron chairman T.H. Tung, speaking at a forum on September 18, likened the current AI race to three sports cars speeding against each other through city streets, prompting calls to slow down.

title: Podcast highlights: iPhone Duo prices undercut expectations as Apple raises old models
snippet: DIGITIMES analyst Luke Lin said on his podcast that the foldable's pricing is more consumer-friendly than expected, but Apple's across-the-board price hikes on older models will weigh on iPhone shipments in the second half of the year. He added that the packaging changes for the A20 Pro are the signal that supply chain players should watch most closely.

title: CHT completes 4th Taiwan-Matsu subsea cable, boosting offshore resilience
snippet: Chunghwa Telecom (CHT) announced on September 18 that the nearly 300km-long Taiwan-Matsu submarine cable has been completed, landed, tested, and has officially been added to the Taiwan-Matsu external communications network. The project strengthens communications resilience for the outlying Matsu Islands by adding a third route with redundant backup and improving service stability for residents and public services.

title: ACM Research's Shanghai unit leans on overseas installs, panel-level plating for its next leg of growth
snippet: ACM Research Shanghai is staking its growth case on two developments: planned tool installations at customers outside mainland China and orders for panel-level advanced packaging equipment, according to Star Market Daily, Securities Times, and East Money.

title: India roundup: Semicon India 2026 puts commercial production and supplier investment in focus
snippet: India's semiconductor push is moving from policy to production, with new government funding, supplier investments, rising deal activity and expanding equipment, materials, testing and manufacturing capacity across the ecosystem nationwide.

title: Analysis: The race to superintelligence meets a demand for restraint — and the industry is split
snippet: The extraordinary technological progress humanity has witnessed since AI first emerged has propelled a fundamental shift in industrial development. With experts hailing AI as the next phase of the digital revolution and an extension of Industry 4.0, the technology is increasingly reshaping how industries operate.

title: Wired vs. wireless internet: Which should you choose for your home?
snippet: Wired and wireless internet are both ways that ISPs deliver service to your home, but one isn't necessarily superior to the other.
